Kettering Health 340B Program Savings Narrative

Kettering Health participates in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as part of its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves. The program allows eligible Kettering Health entities to purchase outpatient medications at reduced prices, generating savings that are reinvested to expand access to care, improve affordability, and strengthen patient services.

Consistent with federal guidance, 340B savings are not maintained as a separate fund but are integrated into the overall financial framework of Kettering Health. These resources are strategically deployed to directly support patient care initiatives, particularly for underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.
Demonstrated Patient and Community Impact in 2025

In 2025, Kettering Health’s patient assistance program supported in part by 340B savings—generated over $91.8 million in total patient support, reflecting a substantial investment in medication access and affordability.
Complementing these efforts, Kettering Health also provided significant levels of uncompensated care across the system, underscoring its role as a safety net provider:
Charity Care: $255.6 million
Bad Debt: $128.6 million
Total Uncompensated Care: $376.5 million
These figures highlight the magnitude of financial support provided to patients and communities and reinforce the critical role 340B savings play in sustaining these efforts.
Key patient assistance highlights include:
Infusion Support: More than $29.3 million in assistance
Specialty Pharmacy Programs: Over $48.5 million in total support
Ambulatory Care Assistance: Approximately $12.8 million
Together, these investments demonstrate how 340B-enabled resources are directly translated into meaningful financial relief and improved access to care.
Expanding Access to Care

Kettering Health uses 340B program savings to broaden access to essential healthcare services. These resources help offset the significant financial burden reflected in the $376.5 million in uncompensated care provided in 2025, enabling:
Continued care regardless of a patient’s ability to pay
Expansion of services in rural and underserved communities
Sustainability of critical programs that operate at a financial loss
Enhancing Medication Access and Affordability
Medication affordability remains a central focus of Kettering Health’s 340B strategy. The 2025 data reflect a comprehensive approach that includes:
Direct financial assistance to reduce patient out-of-pocket costs
Free drug replacement programs ensuring continuity of therapy
Copay support for high-cost infusion and specialty medications
Innovative tools such as the 340B Care Card program
These efforts reduce financial barriers and complement the system’s broader charity care and uncompensated care commitments.
Supporting and Expanding Clinical Services
The breadth of assistance across infusion, specialty, and ambulatory care settings reflects Kettering Health’s investment in comprehensive clinical services. 340B savings help support:
Advanced therapies for complex and chronic conditions
Specialty pharmacy management of high-cost medications
Integrated outpatient care models
These services are essential in managing the needs of patients who may otherwise contribute to uncompensated care if access were limited.
Addressing Social Determinants of Health

Kettering Health recognizes that financial hardship is a major barrier to care. The combination of $91.8 million in patient assistance and $376.5 million in uncompensated care demonstrates a system-wide commitment to reducing these barriers.
Additional support includes transportation, education, and care coordination services that ensure patients can access and adhere to treatment.
Investing in Workforce and Infrastructure
Delivering this level of patient and community support requires significant operational investment. 340B savings fund:
Clinical pharmacy teams and patient assistance coordinators
Infrastructure supporting specialty and infusion services
Technology systems for tracking and optimizing assistance
Compliance oversight and program integrity
Offsetting Financial Pressures and Sustaining Services
The scale of charity care and bad debt in 2025 illustrates the financial realities faced by Kettering Health. 340B savings help offset:
$255.6 million in charity care provided to patients in need
$128.6 million in bad debt associated with unpaid care
Reimbursement shortfalls and high-cost therapies
These resources are essential to sustaining access to care and maintaining critical services across the system.
Advancing Community and Population Health
Through strategic reinvestment of 340B savings, Kettering Health continues to improve community health outcomes by:
Reducing delays in care due to financial barriers
Improving medication adherence
Supporting chronic disease management
Expanding preventive care initiatives
Ensuring Program Integrity and Compliance
Kettering Health is committed to responsible stewardship of the 340B program. Program savings support:
Ongoing audits and monitoring
Staff education and compliance efforts
Policies and systems aligned with federal requirements
Summary
In 2025, Kettering Health demonstrated the impact of its mission-driven approach through:
$91.8 million in patient assistance programs
$376.5 million in total uncompensated care, including:
$255.6 million in charity care
$128.6 million in bad debt
340B program savings are a vital component enabling Kettering Health to sustain these efforts by:
Expanding access to care
Reducing financial barriers for patients
Supporting high-cost and specialized therapies
Strengthening clinical services and infrastructure
Through this reinvestment, Kettering Health continues to fulfill its mission of delivering compassionate, high-quality care while addressing the evolving needs of the communities it serves.
